- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, increase forecast slope to avoid premature pessimism.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.0) and price has recently spiked, apply mean reversion bias to correct overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently above true price over 5+ days with no sentiment signal, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to account for lag.  
- For short-term (1–7 day) horizons, align forecast with sentiment direction; for long-term (10+ day), apply mean reversion to smooth out volatility.
